records.summary: 1237 Polk St is an established bar (McTeague's Saloon) in the Polk Street NCD, holding an active Type 48 license since 2008 under a Conditional Use Authorization granted in 2008 (Motion #17569). The space was previously a restaurant/bar with a Type 47 license dating to 1986. The zoning pathway confirms that a bar is a conditional use on the first story in NCD-POLK, and because an active Type 48 exists at this address the space is read as a bar; the proposal to add entertainment to the existing bar is not a change of use. The block is extremely dense: 31 food/drink businesses and 21 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with 16 bars in that radius. Four dated use decisions for bars, restaurants, and entertainment within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years show 1 approval and 3 approvals with conditions; no denials, but too few cases (N=4) for a meaningful approval rate.

The most recent entertainment CUA on Polk (2019-020049CUA at 1131 Polk, approved 2021) imposed mandatory soundproofing conditions requiring bass and vibrations to be contained and incidental noise to be inaudible beyond the premises. This signals heightened acoustic standards for new entertainment approvals.

Place of Entertainment permits in conjunction with existing bars in NCD-POLK have been recommended for approval by Planning in recent agency referrals (2018-015981MIS at 1160 Polk), indicating departmental support for the entertainment overlay pathway.

Recent entertainment approvals require community liaison appointment, patron behavior signage at exits, and sidewalk maintenance/litter monitoring within a one-block radius as standard operating conditions.
No denials or withdrawals of bar or entertainment CUAs appear in the NCD-POLK candidate set within the past 20 years; all decided use decisions (N=7 CUAs) show approval or approval with conditions.

approvals.summary: A Conditional Use Authorization is required because the existing bar at this address is being intensified by adding entertainment; Planning Code Section 178 prohibits significant alteration or intensification of a conditional use without a new CUA.

findings.text: An active ABC Type 48 license (on-sale general, public premises) is on file at 1237 Polk St, issued June 25, 2008, under the business name McTeague's Saloon.

The bar use at this address was authorized by Conditional Use Authorization case 2007.1281C, approved by the Planning Commission on March 13, 2008 (Motion #17569), under Sections 303, 723.41 and 790.22 for a bar in the Polk NCD.

In NCD-POLK zoning, a bar on the first story is a conditional use under Planning Code Section 723, and a conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without a new Conditional Use per Section 178.

Seven Conditional Use Authorizations for bars or entertainment in NCD-POLK within 150 meters over the last 30 years show all were approved (4 straightforward approvals, 3 with conditions), with zero denials in the candidate set.

The most recent CUA adding entertainment to a bar in NCD-POLK (2019-020049CUA at 1131 Polk St, 102 m away, approved April 2021) imposed mandatory soundproofing conditions requiring incidental noise to be inaudible beyond the premises and bass and vibrations to be contained within the structure.

The description does not state whether the business is part of a chain (formula retail), whether the entertainment will be Limited Live Performance or Place of Entertainment, or whether the proposal changes a condition of the 2008 CUA approval (Motion #17569), so those triggers are not decided.

approvals.summary: The description does not specify what alcohol will be served (beer and wine, or full bar) or how the license will be obtained (continuation of the existing Type 48, or a new or transferred license), so the alcohol license requirements cannot be established.

findings.text: An active Type 48 (on-sale general, public premises) license has been on file at 1237 Polk St since June 25, 2008, which authorizes the sale of beer, wine and distilled spirits for on-premises consumption without a food requirement.

Polk Street is in an extremely high-density area with 21 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet and 57 within 1,000 feet; the density statistics flag undue concentration, which can trigger ABC scrutiny and a Public Convenience or Necessity requirement.

ABC license applications (original or transfer) are referred by ABC to the San Francisco Police Department and Planning Department for review under California Business and Professions Code Section 23987.

approvals.summary: An entertainment permit from the Entertainment Commission is required because the bar will have live entertainment and amplified sound; whether a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit is needed depends on details not yet specified.

findings.text: San Francisco Police Code Section 1060 requires a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit for live performance, DJs, or karaoke; the Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application.

Place of Entertainment permit applications are sent to the Police Department, Planning Department, Department of Building Inspection, Department of Public Health, and Fire Department for review under Police Code Section 1060.2.

Planning Department recommended approval of a Place of Entertainment permit for a bar at 1160 Polk St (118 m away) in December 2018, stating that entertainment in conjunction with an existing bar is conditionally permitted in Polk NCD per Motion 16697.

The Entertainment Commission approved a Limited Live Performance permit for the bar at 1327 Polk St (63 m away) in January 2019, noting it is permitted as an accessory use under Police Code Section 1060.

expected_conditions.condition: Entertainment shall be performed within the enclosed building only; the building shall be adequately soundproofed so that incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises and bass and vibrations are contained within the structure.
expected_conditions.basis: The most recent entertainment CUA at 1131 Polk St (102 m, approved 2021) imposed this exact condition. The 2019-020049CUA decision states nighttime entertainment must be soundproofed so incidental noise is not audible beyond premises and bass and vibrations are contained within the enclosed structure, citing SF Noise Control Ordinance compliance.

expected_conditions.condition: Operating hours for entertainment shall end by 2:00 a.m., consistent with the alcohol service cutoff under California law.
expected_conditions.basis: The concept closes after midnight but before 2 a.m.; Planning Code Section 723 in NCD-POLK sets principally permitted hours 6 a.m.–2 a.m. (conditional 2 a.m.–6 a.m.). Two recent CUAs in NCD-POLK (2016-010348CUA at 1233 Polk and 2018-015319MIS at 1327 Polk) approved operations until 2 a.m. with late-night conditions.

expected_conditions.condition: The operator shall appoint a community liaison to deal with issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties, and provide written notice of the liaison's name and contact to the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019-020049CUA at 1131 Polk St required appointment of a community liaison prior to issuance of a building permit. This is a standard condition for entertainment approvals in residential corridors.

expected_conditions.condition: Notices urging patrons to leave the establishment and neighborhood in a quiet, peaceful, and orderly fashion and to not litter or block driveways shall be well-lit and prominently displayed at all entrances and exits.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019-020049CUA at 1131 Polk St imposed this condition verbatim. It is a standard good-neighbor condition for bars and entertainment venues in NCD zoning.

expected_conditions.condition: The operator shall maintain the main entrance and all sidewalks abutting the property in a clean and sanitary condition and monitor the sidewalk within a one-block radius daily to keep it free of litter associated with the business during business hours.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019-020049CUA at 1131 Polk St required sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius under SF Police Code Article 1, Section 34 and DPW Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. This is a standard eating and drinking use condition.

expected_conditions.condition: Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019-020049CUA at 1131 Polk St imposed this condition, and it is a standard eating and drinking use condition under DPW garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines.

expected_conditions.condition: The Type 48 ABC license shall continue; no upgrade to a more intensive license type is authorized unless a new or amended CUA is obtained.
expected_conditions.basis: Agency referrals at 1327 Polk St (2018-014298MIS, 2018-015319MIS) approved continuation of bar use conditioned on the existing license type only (Type 42 in that case, with no Type 48 allowed per Motion 16946). The 2008 CUA here authorized a Type 48; any change in license type would likely require Planning review.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a copy of Planning Commission Motion #17569 (the 2008 CUA approval for this bar) from SF Planning and review all conditions of approval to determine whether the entertainment proposal changes any condition.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request the full Motion and conditions from case 2007.1281C, approved March 13, 2008. Review with counsel whether adding entertainment is covered by that approval or requires an amendment. If any condition prohibits entertainment or limits the use to a bar without entertainment, the application must address that condition explicitly.

filing_playbook.action: Commission an acoustic study from a qualified engineer to establish baseline sound levels, demonstrate that bass and vibrations will be contained within the structure, and propose soundproofing measures to ensure incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The Planning Commission has imposed strict soundproofing conditions on recent entertainment approvals in NCD-POLK (notably 2019-020049CUA at 1131 Polk St). Submit the acoustic report with the CUA application, showing compliance with the SF Noise Control Ordinance and documenting the proposed insulation, wall construction, and equipment placement to contain bass and vibrations.

filing_playbook.action: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning under Section 303 for intensification of the existing bar by adding entertainment (Section 723.48, Nighttime Entertainment in NCD-POLK), including the acoustic study, a site plan showing the performance area, and a narrative explaini…
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the bar use was approved in 2008 (case 2007.1281C, Motion #17569) and the Type 48 license has been active since June 2008. The proposal is to add live entertainment and amplified sound, closing after midnight but before 2 a.m., within the principally permitted hours (6 a.m.–2 a.m.) for NCD-POLK. Emphasize that the entertainment will be contained within the existing enclosed space, soundproofing will be installed per the acoustic study, and the operator will implement a good-neighbor protocol including community liaison, patron notices at exits, and sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius. Cite the precedent of entertainment approvals at 1233 Polk (1993.422C, 1993), 1101-1127 Polk (2003.0611C, 2003), 1160 Polk (2018-015981MIS, 2018), and 1131 Polk (2019-020049CUA, 2021), all approved in NCD-POLK.

filing_playbook.action: After Planning approval of the CUA, file an application with the SF Entertainment Commission for a Place of Entertainment permit or Limited Live Performance permit (depending on the entertainment scope confirmed with Planning), including the approved CUA, the acoustic study, and proof of the bar's…
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the entertainment use is authorized by the Planning Commission CUA (cite the case number and motion). Provide the acoustic study demonstrating soundproofing compliance and the good-neighbor operating plan. If the entertainment is limited to a small performance area (200 sq ft or less) ending by 10 or 11 p.m., request a Limited Live Performance permit; otherwise request a Place of Entertainment permit. Commit to posting patron behavior notices at all exits, maintaining a community liaison, and ensuring the building is soundproofed so incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises.

filing_playbook.action: If the alcohol service will change (e.g., from Type 48 to a different license type, or a new or transferred license), file the ABC application or transfer with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control and request zoning sign-off from SF Planning as part of the ABC referral process.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the bar use is conditionally permitted per the 2008 CUA (Motion #17569) and the Type 48 license has been active since 2008. If continuing the Type 48, confirm with Planning that no new ABC referral is needed. If transferring or upgrading the license, submit the ABC application with the lease, the CUA approval, and the seller's permit, and note that ABC will refer the application to Planning and Police under Business and Professions Code Section 23987. Address the high-density area (21 on-sale licenses within 500 ft) by emphasizing the existing license history and good-neighbor commitments to mitigate any undue concentration concerns.

filing_playbook.action: If tenant improvements will be made (soundproofing, stage or performance area build-out, or any structural or mechanical work), file a building permit application with SF Department of Building Inspection after the CUA is approved, including the acoustic plans, the CUA approval, and a code analysis…
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the work implements the approved CUA for entertainment intensification. If the occupancy group remains A-2 (Assembly) or B (under 50 people), confirm that with DBI plan check. Include the acoustic plans showing soundproofing construction details, and route the permit to Planning (automatic under Section 175), Health (for kitchen and food service), and Fire (if occupant load is 50 or more, for Place of Assembly permit). Confirm that the existing hood, grease interceptor, and FOG registration are on file and will not be altered, or include them in the permit if new work affects the kitchen.

filing_playbook.action: File an application for a Health Permit to Operate with SF Department of Public Health if the food service scope or kitchen layout changes, or confirm with DPH that the existing permit covers the entertainment intensification.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the bar serves limited food (limited cooking type) and the entertainment addition does not change the food preparation scope. If the existing health permit is on file and the kitchen is not altered, request confirmation from DPH that no new permit is needed. If the permit must be updated, submit the application with the Business Account Number, the approved CUA, and the food safety manager certificate, and schedule the pre-opening inspection after any tenant improvement work is substantially complete.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses before opening to cover live entertainment and recorded music under federal copyright law.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online for both licenses (the two catalogs do not overlap, so both are needed for a general mix of music). The annual fee is formula-based on occupancy and music use. State the bar's occupancy, the entertainment schedule (live and recorded music), and the days per week of operation. The licenses are effective immediately upon approval and are required before the first entertainment performance.

timeline_cost.notes: This timeline and cost covers the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 including CPI adjustment and any construction-related fee increase), the Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800), and the Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000) if a new permit is needed. The CUA is the critical path: the Entertainment Commission permit cannot be filed until the CUA is approved, and building permits for soundproofing cannot be issued until the CUA is effective. The ranges assume approval. If the CUA or entertainment permit is denied or must be withdrawn, no time or cost for those approvals is incurred and the project cannot proceed as described. The 8 comparable CUA decisions for bars or entertainment in NCD-POLK took 7 to 538 days from filing to approval (N=8 approved cases), with the most recent entertainment CUA (2019-020049CUA) taking 538 days (filed October 2019, approved April 2021). Alcohol license cost is not included because the description does not state what license transaction is proposed; if the existing Type 48 continues with no ABC action, there is no ABC filing cost. Building permit cost is not included because the scope of tenant improvements is not stated; typical soundproofing and performance area build-out costs $800–$15,000 in permit fees depending on construction valuation. ASCAP and BMI licenses ($600–$5,000 combined annually) are operational costs, not government fees, and are excluded here. The timeline assumes no appeals; a CUA appeal adds 30+ days after the Commission hearing.
